thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool eu-west-1/gpu-pool-A reports sustained queue depth > 25k and 429 spike across tiered routes. Paging @oncall and @sre. Auto-scale attempts failing with 'max_replicas reached' errors. See monitor: https://grafana.redwood/prod/boards/987
ashok: acked. I'm oncall. grabbing list of impacted routes now. initial guess: token-bucket throttling + autoscale ceiling.
maria: seeing a huge burst from /v1/chat on standard-tier — 95% 429s. enterprise-tier mostly fine. Metrics: median latency up, 429 rate 18% over last 10m.
ashok: pulling autoscaler logs now. shows repeated ScaleUp request -> rejected by pool controller: "requested_replicas > max_replicas". pool config max_replicas=6 but traffic would need ~18 to drain.
kevin: wait, why is max_replicas 6? that was set for cost controls last week for that pool. we should be able to override in emergencies.
maria: also discovered token-bucket capacity for 'standard' tier is 1000 tokens/min in redis, but typical steady-state demand is ~20k/min — looks like an order-of-magnitude misconfig.
jen: this is bad. customers are getting 429s. Who's owning customer comms? Product/CS?
elaine: cc @support — we're manually paging highest-impact customers. CS is sending brief. We'll need ETA for mitigation.
ashok: mitigation plan (live):
1) temporarily bump pool max_replicas to 20 for eu-west-1/gpu-pool-A
2) relax token-bucket for standard-tier to 25000/min
3) enable fallback route -> small-quantized model (gpt-small-q4) for non-enterprise traffic
4) if autoscaler still refuses, scale manually via k8s
I will execute 1 and 2 now.
ops-runner: runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/gpu-saturation-runbook
ashok: running command: ```kubectl -n redwood patch gpupool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-A -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":20}}' --type=merge``` returning: patched.
maria: patched. Grafana shows scale target allowed now.
ashok: updating rate limiter config in redis. applying patch: ```
REDIS> HSET rate_limit:tiers:standard capacity 25000
REDIS> HSET rate_limit:tiers:standard refill_rate 25000
``` updated.
kevin: making quick config change to route:lower-priority -> fallback model. ```curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/routes/route-std-001/actions -d '{"action":"set_fallback","model":"gpt-small-q4"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'``` response 202.
maria: enabling fallback reduces queue growth, 429 rate down to 7% in 5m.
ashok: autoscaler still slow. starting manual node add: ```kubectl scale --replicas=18 gpupool/eu-west-1-gpu-pool-A -n redwood``` note: this bypasses autoscaler temporarily.
jen: handoff note for next oncall (evening): we've applied emergency overrides: max_replicas=20, token-bucket standard=25000, fallback to small model enabled. Main root cause appears to be misconfig of standard-tier token-bucket + conservative pool max_replicas. If we hit resource limits again, consider rerouting heavy customers to dedicated.
elaine: CS update sent to customers A, B, and C — we're offering temporary quota bumps and priority routing. ETA to stable: ~20-40m while caches warm and new replicas spin up.
kevin: small note: autoscaler cooldown was set to 15m and aggressive scale down also triggered earlier which prevented scaling up. I'll file a follow-up to default to 60s cooldown for scale-up windows under saturation.
ashok: confirming status: queue depth trending down from 25k -> 6k. 429s now 3% and falling. latency still elevated for a fraction of requests.
incident-bot: incident severity updated to SEV2. timeline started 1787659999. Assigned responders: ashok, maria, kevin. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/gpu-saturation-runbook
jen: handoff to evening oncall @jen — oncall slack DM me for checklist. I'll leave notes in the runbook and create a support ticket for postmortem.
maria: quick logs showing token-bucket reject messages cleared after HSET. sample:
```
[2026-02-12T18:45:12Z] rate_limiter: tier=standard request_id=abc123 action=throttle reason=out_of_tokens
[2026-02-12T18:50:01Z] rate_limiter: tier=standard request_id=def456 action=allow tokens=24990
```
ashok: root-cause hypothesis: two simultaneous missteps — (1) token-bucket capacity scaled down accidentally in last config roll (regexp bug in deploy script), (2) pool max_replicas intentionally low for cost controls but not part of SLO emergency overrides. When traffic spiked, the throttler started returning 429s before autoscaler could effectively scale due to the low ceiling.
kevin: what's next actions list for postmortem? I'll open an RFC. Draft:
- revert slippery deploy script fix and add integration test for tier config regex
- add emergency policy to allow oncall to raise pool max_replicas via control-plane for 1h
- default autoscaler scale-up cooldown to 60s under high-queue condition
- add canary test for token-bucket values during deploys
- run a load test that simulates standard-tier 10k qps steady-state
jen: I'll own the postmortem. tagging: oncall, infra, product, cs.
elaine: CS will follow up with impacted customers with detailed timeline once pm review is done.
ashok: marking incident as mitigated for now. leaving open for postmortem and clean-up. Please revert emergency overrides only after PMT/infra agrees on safe values. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity SEV2. Last update 1787662200.
